title: Mark the Soft Falling Snow
description: Mark the Soft Falling Snow in Tonic Solfa to BELSIZE, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Philip Doddridge wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 169, “The Gospel”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Hallelujah Metre (6.6.6.6.4.4.4.4), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to BELSIZE; any other Hallelujah Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Mark the soft fall-ing snow And the dif-fu-sive rain! To heaven, from whence it fell, It turns not back a-gain; Till, wa-tering earth Through ev-ery pore, It calls forth all Her se-cret store.

lines: To heaven, from whence it fell,
And man and beast are fed

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Philip Doddridge died in 1751.
credits: Words by Philip Doddridge (1702–1751), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to BELSIZE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
